scope: Close every exact Java public-int OnSkill* event callback so Publish 14.1 skill-box and skill-modifier changes cannot wake inherited NGE progression, reward, profession, Beast Master, level, or template authority while retained Force-sensitive, Jedi trial, Force Rank, Creature Handler/familiar cosmetic, Tansarii, badge, JTL, novice-quest, Squad Leader, HAM-pool, defensive-mod presentation, movement-immunity, Aim, Tumble, and command behavior continues to work.

findings: Publish 14.1 skill awards may legitimately update commands, badges, Jedi Force Rank titles, Creature Handler state, JTL pilot setup, and tutorial presentation.
NGE skill families, passive class runtimes, Spy runtime, and Beast Master player state must be rejected or cleaned before any normal skill-grant effect executes.
Publish 14.1 skill revocation legitimately recalculates Force power, retires lost JTL and Squad Leader state, refreshes certification, and maintains Jedi trial and Force Rank eligibility.

A complete lifecycle inventory is required because a listener can bypass otherwise-correct centralized skill admission or surrender through grant, revoke, pre-grant, pre-revoke, modifier-expiry, modifier-change, or template-change side effects.
The Force-sensitive kickoff listener must detach with the canonical quest.force_sensitive.fs_kickoff script identifier on initialize, attach, login, and full Force-sensitive cleanup.
